subject.title: Heartbeat skipped reason 'target-none' is misleading when delivery is disabled by default

question: Should OpenClaw preserve `reason: "target-none"` as the machine-readable contract and add a human-readable disabled-delivery hint, or rename the reason itself?
rationale: Both viable fixes touch user-visible diagnostic contract: a rename is clearer but can break parsers, while an additive hint keeps compatibility but expands the event/status surface.

options.title: Add an additive hint
options.body: Keep `reason: "target-none"`, add a disabled-delivery hint or equivalent display field, and update CLI/status formatting and tests.

options.title: Rename the reason
options.body: Change the machine reason to a clearer value like `delivery-disabled`, accepting the compatibility cost for any consumers parsing the old value.

options.title: Leave current output
options.body: Keep `target-none` unchanged and rely on docs, accepting the existing operator confusion as low-priority UX friction.

recommendation.title: Add an additive hint
recommendation.body: Keep `reason: "target-none"`, add a disabled-delivery hint or equivalent display field, and update CLI/status formatting and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the default-none behavior and have the strongest history across the affected heartbeat, outbound, and status surfaces.
